quotes.text: The real problem is that you cannot audit a mouse click. You cannot roll back a mouse click.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints why manual portal provisioning fails at scale.

quotes.text: Infrastructure as code means describing your infrastructure in a file that Azure can read and build for you. That is it. One sentence.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear one-sentence definition of infrastructure as code.

quotes.text: The real superpower of IAC is not the template format itself. It is not bicep versus ARM versus Terraform. The real superpower is version control.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts the focus from tool debates to the actual benefit.

quotes.text: Write your IAC as if someone else will maintain it six months from now because that someone else is probably you and you will have forgotten everything.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable, practical advice on maintainable templates.

quotes.text: When you use IAC, security is not something you add later. It is baked into the template from the start.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames infrastructure as code as security by design.

takeaways: Infrastructure as code describes the desired end state of an Azure environment in a file, so every deployment produces the same result without configuration drift.
For Azure-only teams, Bicep is the easiest starting point because it compiles to ARM templates and is natively supported by Microsoft.
Store templates in version control, keep secrets in Azure Key Vault, run what-if before deploying and never bypass the pipeline for quick portal fixes.
hook: Clicking through the Azure portal for every environment invites mistakes and drift between dev, test and production. This episode explains infrastructure as code for Azure admins and beginners, compares ARM templates, Bicep and Terraform, and shows a safe way to get started.
